docs.title: Hazbin Tracker
docs.text:
A tray app that watches the Hazbin Hotel store for new trading cards.

It runs in the background, checks the store periodically and tells you when cards were published since the last check. By default it shows a desktop notification, and it can also send a push notification to your phone through Pushover.

  • User Guide: install, use and configure the app.
  • Developer Guide: set up the project, how it is built, tested and released.

def build_open_track_file_action(self) -> QtGui.QAction:
    """Build the action to open the track file.

    Returns:
        QtGui.QAction: The action to open the track file.
    """
    action = QtGui.QAction("Track File", self)
    action.setToolTip("Open the track file")

    action.triggered.connect(
        lambda: QtGui.QDesktopServices.openUrl(
            QtCore.QUrl.fromLocalFile(self.TRACK_FILE_PATH)
        )

def create_cache(self):
    """Create cache file with current cards data and last check time."""
    LOGGER.debug("Creating cache")
    cache_content = {
        "last_check_time": self.last_check_time.isoformat(),
        "cards": [card.model_dump(mode="json") for card in self.cards_data],
    }
    with self.TRACK_FILE_PATH.open("w") as cache_file:
        json.dump(cache_content, cache_file, indent=4)

def fetch_cards_data_from_cache(self):
    """Fetch cards data from cache file."""
    LOGGER.debug("Loading cards from cache")
    with self.TRACK_FILE_PATH.open() as cache_file:
        cache_data = json.load(cache_file)
    self._cards_data = self._load_cards(cache_data.get("cards", []))
    self.record_time(
        time_override=datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(
            cache_data.get("last_check_time")
        )
    )
    LOGGER.debug(f"Loaded {len(self._cards_data)} cards from {self.TRACK_FILE_PATH}")

def find_new_cards(self, source_cards: list[HazbinCard]) -> list[HazbinCard]:
    """Get cards published after the last check.

    Args:
        source_cards (list[HazbinCard]): cards fetched from the source

    Returns:
        list[HazbinCard]: cards published after the last check time
    """
    if self.last_check_time is None:
        return []
    return [
        card for card in source_cards if card.published_at > self.last_check_time
    ]

def generate_new_cards_message(self, new_cards: list[HazbinCard]) -> str:
    """Generate a message for new cards found.

    Args:
        new_cards (list[HazbinCard]): list of new cards found
    Returns:
        str: generated message
    """
    LOGGER.debug("Generating new cards message...")
    message = f"Found {len(new_cards)} new Hazbin card(s):"
    for card in new_cards:
        suffix = "" if card.is_available else "(Not Available)"
        message += f"\n- {card.title} {suffix}"
    return message

def on_new_cards_found(self, new_cards: list):
    """Handle new cards found event.

    Args:
        new_cards (list): list of new cards found
    """
    if not self.pushover_config_values.enabled:
        LOGGER.debug("Push notifications are disabled, skipping...")
        return

    try:
        send_notification(
            app_key=self.pushover_config_values.app_key,
            user_key=self.pushover_config_values.user_key,
            title="HazbinTracker - New Card(s) available!",
            message=self.generate_new_cards_message(new_cards),
        )
    except PushoverError:
        LOGGER.exception("Failed to send Pushover notification for new cards.")
    except Exception:
        LOGGER.exception(
            "Failed to send Pushover notification due to unhandled error."
        )

def record_check_result(self, new_cards: list[HazbinCard]):
    """Record the result of a check.

    Args:
        new_cards (list[HazbinCard]): list of new cards found
    """
    record = {
        "timestamp": self.nice_last_checked_time,
        "new_cards": [card.model_dump(mode="json") for card in new_cards],
    }
    if CHECK_HISTORY_FILE_PATH.exists():
        try:
            history = json.loads(CHECK_HISTORY_FILE_PATH.read_text())
        except Exception:
            LOGGER.warning("Failed to read check history file, starting fresh.")
            history = []
    else:
        history = []

    history.insert(0, record)

    # Trim history if it exceeds the maximum size
    history = history[: self.config_values.history_size]
    CHECK_HISTORY_FILE_PATH.write_text(json.dumps(history, indent=4))
    LOGGER.debug(f"Recorded check result to history: {CHECK_HISTORY_FILE_PATH}")

def record_time(self, time_override: datetime.datetime | None = None):
    """Record the current time as last check time.

    Args:
        time_override (datetime.datetime, optional): time to set as last check time.
            Defaults to None, which uses the current time.
    """
    LOGGER.debug("Recording time...")
    new_time = (
        time_override if time_override else datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)
    )
    self.last_check_time = new_time
    LOGGER.debug(f"Recorded time: {self.last_check_time}")

def run_check(self) -> bool:
    """Start a check for new cards in the background.

    Returns:
        bool: True if a check was started, False if one is already running
    """
    if self.is_check_running:
        LOGGER.debug("Check already in progress, skipping")
        return False
    LOGGER.info("Running cards check...")
    worker = CheckWorker()
    worker.signals.finished.connect(self._on_check_finished)
    worker.signals.failed.connect(self._on_check_failed)
    self._check_worker = worker
    QtCore.QThreadPool.globalInstance().start(worker)
    return True

def start_periodic_check_timer(self):
    """Start the periodic check timer."""
    LOGGER.debug("Starting check timer...")
    if self._check_timer.isActive():
        self._check_timer.stop()
    self._check_timer.setInterval(
        self.config_values.frequency_min * 60 * 1000
    )  # minutes in msƒ
    self._check_timer.start()
    LOGGER.debug(f"Check Timer: {self._check_timer.interval()}ms")

Source code in src/hazbin_tracker/core/cards_tracker.py 
def run(self):
    """Fetch the cards and report the outcome through signals."""
    try:
        cards = self._scraper.get_all_cards()
    except ScraperError as exc:
        self.signals.failed.emit(str(exc))
        return
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - nothing may escape a worker thread
        LOGGER.exception("Unexpected error during cards check")
        self.signals.failed.emit(str(exc))
        return
    self.signals.finished.emit(cards)

def get_app_config() -> HazbinAppConfig:
    """Get the config of the running application.

    Returns:
        HazbinAppConfig: config the application loaded at startup, so it has the
            values of the user's config file. Without an application a new config is
            created and resolved.
    """
    config = getattr(QtCore.QCoreApplication.instance(), "config", None)
    if config is None:
        config = HazbinAppConfig()
        config.resolve()
    return config

def init_handlers(self):
    """Initialize logging handlers."""
    if self.hasHandlers():
        return

    if self.STD_HANDLER:
        stream_handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)
        stream_handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter(self.STD_OUT_FORMAT))

def send_notification(app_key: str, user_key: str, title: str, message: str) -> None:
    """Send a push notification.

    Args:
        app_key (str): API token of the Pushover application.
        user_key (str): Pushover user key to notify.
        title (str): Notification title.
        message (str): Notification text.

    Raises:
        PushoverError: If the request fails or Pushover rejects it.
    """
    try:
        response = requests.post(
            MESSAGES_URL,
            data={
                "token": app_key,
                "user": user_key,
                "title": title,
                "message": message,
            },
            timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT,
        )
        response.raise_for_status()
    except requests.RequestException as exc:
        raise PushoverError(f"Failed to send Pushover notification: {exc}") from exc

def validate_keys(app_key: str, user_key: str) -> bool:
    """Check the keys with Pushover without sending a notification.

    Args:
        app_key (str): API token of the Pushover application.
        user_key (str): Pushover user key.

    Returns:
        bool: True if the keys are valid and the user has an active device,
            False if Pushover rejected them.

    Raises:
        PushoverError: If Pushover can't be reached or fails.
    """
    try:
        response = requests.post(
            VALIDATE_URL,
            data={"token": app_key, "user": user_key},
            timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT,
        )
    except requests.RequestException as exc:
        raise PushoverError(f"Failed to reach Pushover: {exc}") from exc
    if response.status_code == REJECTED_STATUS:
        LOGGER.warning(f"Pushover rejected the keys: {response.text}")
        return False
    try:
        response.raise_for_status()
    except requests.RequestException as exc:
        raise PushoverError(f"Pushover validation failed: {exc}") from exc
    return True

def fetch_products(self) -> list[dict]:
    """Fetch every product page of the cards collection.

    Returns:
        list[dict]: Raw product dictionaries.
    """
    products = []
    page = 1
    while True:
        page_products = self._fetch_page(page)
        products.extend(page_products)
        LOGGER.info(f"Page {page}: {len(page_products)} products")
        if len(page_products) < self.config.page_limit:
            return products
        page += 1
        time.sleep(self.config.page_delay)

def get_all_cards(self) -> list[HazbinCard]:
    """Get all trading cards sorted by the configured sort key.

    Products that are not valid cards (e.g. not published) are skipped.

    Returns:
        list[HazbinCard]: Cards, newest first by default.

    Raises:
        ScraperError: If the cards can't be fetched.
    """
    cards = []
    for product in self.fetch_products():
        try:
            cards.append(HazbinCard.model_validate(self._clean_title(product)))
        except ValidationError as exc:
            LOGGER.warning(f"Skipping product {product.get('id')}: {exc}")
    return sorted(
        cards, key=lambda card: getattr(card, self.config.sort_key), reverse=True
    )

def __init__(self, parent: QtCore.QObject = None):
    """Instance constructor.

    Args:

    super().__init__(parent)
    self.setWindowTitle("About Hazbin Tracker")

    layout = QtWidgets.QVBoxLayout(self)

    # Icon at the top

    icon = QtGui.QIcon(":/icons/hazbin.png")
    pixmap = icon.pixmap(64, 64)
    icon_label.setPixmap(pixmap)
    icon_label.setAlignment(QtCore.Qt.AlignCenter)
    layout.addWidget(icon_label)

    # Title

    title_label.setAlignment(QtCore.Qt.AlignCenter)
    layout.addWidget(title_label)

    # Version & developer info

        (
            f"Version {QtWidgets.QApplication.applicationVersion()}<br>"
            f"Developed by {AUTHOR_NAME}<br>© {RELEASE_YEAR}"

def lock_check(self):
    """Check for existing application instance using a lock file."""
    self.lock_file = QtCore.QLockFile(self.LOCK_FILE.as_posix())

def center_dialog_on_screen(dialog: QtWidgets.QWidget) -> None:
    """Center the given dialog on the primary screen.

    Args:
        dialog (QtWidgets.QDialog): The dialog to center.
    """
    screen_geometry = QtWidgets.QApplication.primaryScreen().availableGeometry()
    x = (screen_geometry.width() - dialog.width()) // 2
    y = (screen_geometry.height() - dialog.height()) // 2
    dialog.move(x, y)

def data(self, index: QtCore.QModelIndex, role: int) -> typing.Any:
    """Get data for a given index and role.

    Args:
        index (QtCore.QModelIndex): The index to retrieve data for.
        role (int, optional): The role for which data is requested.

    Returns:
        Any: The data for the given index and role.
    """
    if not index.isValid():
        return None

    record = self._records[index.row()]

    if role == QtCore.Qt.ItemDataRole.DisplayRole:
        if index.column() == 0:
            return record.get("timestamp", "")

        if index.column() == 1:
            return self.format_record_new_cards(record)

    return None

def format_record_new_cards(self, record: dict) -> str:
    """Format the new cards list for display.

    Args:
        record (dict): A record containing check info.

    Returns:
        str: Formatted string of new cards.
    """
    new_cards = record.get("new_cards", [])
    if not new_cards:
        return "No new cards"
    result_string = ""
    for card_info in new_cards:
        card_title = card_info.get("title")
        result_string += f"- {card_title}\n"
    return result_string.strip()

Source code in src/hazbin_tracker/ui/models/check_history.py 
def rowCount(self, parent=QtCore.QModelIndex()) -> int:
    """Get the number of rows in the model.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
The project uses uv and Python 3.14 (pinned in .python-version).

uv sync --locked --dev

Run the app from source:

uv run python -m hazbin_tracker.main

The VS Code launch configuration HazbinTracker does the same and reads .env. Set HAZBIN_DEBUG=1 to turn on debug logging.

docs.title: Make targets
docs.text:
The Makefile includes shared targets from sowwic/makefiles, fetched into .make/ (committed). make update-make fetches them again and make help lists every target.

Target What it does make check Lint and tests make lint, make lint-fix, make format Ruff on src and tests make pytest, make pytest-pdb Run the tests, optionally dropping into pdb on failure make qrc Regenerate resources_rc.py from resources.qrc make bundle, make app Build dist/HazbinTracker.app with PyInstaller make install Copy the built app to /Applications make iconset Regenerate the .icns icon from hazbin.png make pushover-check Validate the Pushover keys of your config, no notification is sent make mkdocs Serve these docs

Run a single test with uv run pytest tests/test_tracker.py::test_name. On a headless machine set QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen, which CI does as well.

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
The distribution on PyPI is sowwic-hazbin-tracker, but the import package is hazbin_tracker (module-name under [tool.uv.build-backend] in pyproject.toml).

  • Architecture
  • Building and releasing

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Google-style docstrings (Args:, Returns:, Raises:), which the API reference is built from.
  • Ruff with a line length of 89.
  • develop is the default and pull request branch, master is the release branch.
  • User visible changes are recorded in CHANGELOG.rst.
  • Dependabot opens its pull requests against develop.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: The app is a PySide6 tray application. A timer asks the scraper for the store's cards off the GUI thread, the result is compared with the cards seen before, and the outcome is reported to the user through Qt signals.

docs.title: core.scrapper
docs.text: CardsScraper pages through the store's products.json with curl_cffi (impersonating a browser, as the store rejects plain clients), with a delay between pages and retries with exponential backoff. It raises ScraperError, or RateLimitedError when the store keeps answering 429. Its tunables are in core/constants.py and in the ScraperConfig dataclass.

docs.title: core.cards_tracker
docs.text:
CardsTracker is a QObject that:

  • owns the QTimer of the periodic check (start_periodic_check_timer, which is also called again when the config changes),
  • runs a CheckWorker (a QRunnable) on the thread pool, so a slow request never blocks the UI,
  • compares the fetched cards with track_data.json and records the result in check_history.json,
  • sends the Pushover message when enabled,
  • emits new_cards_found, check_completed, check_failed and repeated_checks_failed (after MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILED_CHECKS failures in a row).

docs.title: core.config
docs.text: HazbinAppConfig is a json-config LayeredConfig with a single root layer backed by config.json. The values are pydantic models (HazbinAppConfigValues with PushoverConfigValues and CardsTrackerConfigValues as nested categories). get_app_config() returns the config of the running application.

docs.title: ui
docs.text:
• HazbinTrackerApplication creates the config, the tracker and the tray icon, and prevents a second instance with a lock file. Its configChanged signal tells the tracker to restart its timer.
  • tray.py holds the tray icon and its menu. It only reacts to tracker signals.
  • The settings editor is ConfigEditorDialog of json-config-qt showing the app config. Saving a layer emits configChanged.
  • check_history_dialog.py and about_dialog.py are plain dialogs.

New behavior usually means a new tracker signal and a slot on the tray or a dialog.

docs.title: version
docs.text: version.py reads the VERSION file, from the project root or from the PyInstaller bundle (sys._MEIPASS) when frozen. The spec bundles VERSION as data.

docs.title: User files
docs.text: All user files live in the directory defined as APP_DATA_DIR in core/constants.py: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/HazbinTracker (~/.config/HazbinTracker) on macOS and Linux, the platform data directory on Windows. On macOS the files of the former location (~/Library/Application Support/HazbinTracker) are moved there on first start.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text: The API reference is generated from the docstrings by mkdocs-autoapi and mkdocstrings.

docs.title: Building the app
docs.text:
make bundle      # or: make app

This compiles the Qt resources and runs PyInstaller with HazbinTracker.spec, producing dist/HazbinTracker.app. The app has no Dock icon (LSUIElement), and its version comes from the VERSION file. make install copies it to /Applications.

Only macOS is built.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
Releases are cut from the master branch.

  1. Add a v x.y.z entry to CHANGELOG.rst.
  2. Put the version in VERSION and run make update-version to sync pyproject.toml (uv.lock too).
  3. Commit and merge to master.
  4. From a clean, up to date master run:

sh make release VERSION=x.y.z

make release runs release.py of sowwic/gh-workflows. It checks that the changelog has the entry, that VERSION and pyproject.toml match and that the version is higher than the latest tag. Then it tags vx.y.z, pushes the tag and merges master back into develop.

Pushing the tag triggers two workflows:

  • Release creates the GitHub release with the changelog entry as its notes.
  • Build app builds the app on a macOS runner, zips it as HazbinTracker-<version>-macos-<arch>.zip and attaches it to that release.

docs.title: CI
docs.text:
Workflow When What unit_tests.yml push, pull request pytest on Ubuntu and Windows (shared python-tests.yml) code_quality.yml pull request Ruff (shared python-lint.yml) deploy_docs.yml push to master publishes these docs to GitHub Pages (shared mkdocs-deploy.yml) release.yml tag v* GitHub release (shared release.yml) build_app.yml tag v*, pull requests touching the build files builds the macOS app, attaches it to the release

The shared workflows come from sowwic/gh-workflows.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Only macOS is supported.

  1. Download HazbinTracker-<version>-macos-<arch>.zip from the latest release.
  2. Unzip it and move HazbinTracker.app to your Applications folder.
  3. Launch it. If macOS refuses to open the app because it is from an unidentified developer, right click it and choose Open.

The app has no Dock icon and no window. It lives in the menu bar, and only one copy runs at a time.

docs.title: The tray menu
docs.text:
Once the app is running this icon appears in the menu bar:

Clicking it opens a menu with:

  • Last checked: when the last check ran.
  • Check for New Cards: run a check now. A manual check tells you when it found nothing or failed.
  • History...: the results of previous checks.
  • Settings...: the settings editor, see Settings.
  • About...
  • Quit

Checks also run in the background, by default every 60 minutes. When new cards are found a notification is shown, and clicking it opens the Hazbin Hotel store in your browser.

If 5 checks in a row fail (for example the store is blocking requests), the app shows a warning that new cards may be missed until the problem is resolved.

docs.title: Check History
docs.text: The history dialog lists the checks that ran in the background, and what each of them found.

docs.title: Where the files are
docs.text:
Everything lives in ~/.config/HazbinTracker (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/HazbinTracker when that is set):

File Content config.json Your settings, see Settings track_data.json The cards seen by the last check and the time it ran check_history.json The check history shown by the history dialog hazbin.log Application log, useful when reporting a problem

Versions before the move to this location stored these in ~/Library/Application Support/HazbinTracker. The files are moved to the new location the first time the app starts.

docs.title: More
docs.text:
• Settings
  • Pushover notifications

docs.title: Pushover notifications
docs.text:
To receive push notifications on your phone:

  1. Register a new application on the Pushover website. This gives you an API token.
  2. Open Settings... from the tray menu and set pushover.app_key to that API token and pushover.user_key to your user key (shown on the front page of the Pushover website).
  3. Set pushover.enabled to true and save.
  4. Install the Pushover app on your phone.

You will now get a push notification when new cards are published, along with the desktop one.

Pushover apps:

  • App Store
  • Play Store

docs.title: Testing the notifications
docs.text:
1. Quit the app.
  2. In ~/.config/HazbinTracker/track_data.json set last_check_time to a much older date.
  3. Launch the app and run Check for New Cards from the tray menu.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Settings... in the tray menu opens a config editor: a tree of all values with their types, where you edit a value in place. Use Save to write the change to your config file, and Undo / Redo to step back. The editor is not modal, so the app keeps working while it is open. Closing it with unsaved changes asks what to do with them.

Saved changes apply right away, there is no need to restart the app. Changing the check frequency restarts the check timer.

docs.title: Available settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Meaning cards_tracker.frequency_min 60 Minutes between background checks. At least 1. cards_tracker.history_size 20 How many checks to keep in the history. At least 10. pushover.enabled false Send a push notification when new cards are found. pushover.user_key empty Your Pushover user key. pushover.app_key empty The API token of your Pushover application.

Please do not set the frequency too low. The store rate limits requests, and a failed check is only retried on the next scheduled one.

docs.title: Editing the file directly
docs.text:
The settings are stored in ~/.config/HazbinTracker/config.json, you can also edit that file with a text editor while the app is not running:

{
  "cards_tracker": {
    "frequency_min": 60,
    "history_size": 20
  },
  "pushover": {
    "enabled": false,
    "user_key": "",
    "app_key": ""
  }
}

Only the values that differ from the defaults are written to the file.
